newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to watch - July 9.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to watch - July 9.

text.p: -- Motorola Inc posted better-than-expected second quarter operating results. The company earned $0.62 per share, excluding a $170 million charge for phasing out its dynamic random access memory (DRAM) business, compared to a First Call consensus estimate of $0.56 and the year-earlier $0.54. Revenues rose 10 percent to $7.5 billion. Motorola shares last traded at 82-3/4.

-- Advanced Micro Devices Inc reported weaker-than-expected second quarter profits, reflecting the rapid shift toward newer-generation semiconductors and pricing pressures on older models. It earned $0.07 per diluted share, compared with a First Call consensus estimate of $0.22. The stock closed at 39-1/8, then fell to 36-5/8 in after-hours trading.
-- McDonald's Corp is expected to name five new division presidents today, to be responsible for increasing domestic business, the Wall Street Journal reported. The stock closed at 48-3/4.

-- Compaq Computer Corp is expected to reduce corporate personal computer prices in a bid to halt gains by rival Dell Computer Corp, the Wall Street Journal said. Compaq closed at 119-9/16 while Dell closed at 127-3/4.

-- The White House will reject a key element of the proposed $368 billion tobacco settlement because it would impose new restrictions on federal authority to regulate nicotine in cigarettes, the Washington Post reported. Philip Morris Cos Inc closed at 44-7/16 and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp closed at 32-3/4.
